meaning: Emergency stopping is emergency switching used specifically to stop an operation.
studyNote: It is focused on bringing dangerous motion or operation to a stop rather than necessarily isolating every source for maintenance.
distinction: Emergency stopping is a purpose within emergency switching; isolation is a separate safety function.

meaning: Emergency switching is an operation intended to remove an unexpected danger as quickly as possible.
studyNote: The control must be suited to the hazard it is intended to remove and must be distinguishable from routine functional switching.
distinction: Functional switching is for normal operation; emergency switching is for unexpected danger.

meaning: Functional switching is normal operational switching used to turn electrical energy on or off, or vary it, for all or part of an installation.
studyNote: It is used to control normal service rather than to establish safe isolation or respond to an emergency.
distinction: Functional switching, emergency switching and isolation have different purposes even if some equipment can perform more than one function.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide has a dedicated functional-switching section and distinguishes it from devices used only for isolation or off-load functions.

meaning: Inspection is examination of an electrical installation using the senses as appropriate, before relying on instrument tests to find matters that can be established visually or otherwise by direct examination.
studyNote: Inspection checks selection, erection, identification, damage, accessibility and other visible or directly observable aspects of the installation.
distinction: Testing uses measurements or test procedures; inspection is the examination stage and normally precedes testing.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide states that inspection precedes testing and gives a checklist covering conductor connections, identification, routing, protective measures, devices and documentation.

meaning: An instructed person is someone who has been adequately advised or is adequately supervised by a skilled person so they can recognize electrical risks and avoid the hazards relevant to the work.
studyNote: The status depends on the instruction or supervision and the hazards of the task; it is not simply a job title.
distinction: A skilled person has the required education, training and practical skills independently for the relevant work; an ordinary person is neither skilled nor instructed.

meaning: Maintenance is the combination of technical and administrative actions, including supervision, used to keep an item able to perform its required function or restore it to that condition.
studyNote: It includes both preventive actions and restoration after deterioration or failure, not just physical repair.

meaning: Minor works are additions or alterations that do not extend to providing a new circuit, according to the supplied historical definition.
studyNote: The term distinguishes limited work on existing circuits from work that creates a new circuit.
distinction: The certification and legal treatment of work must be checked against the current applicable rules; this entry preserves the supplied 2015 study definition.

meaning: An ordinary person is someone who is neither a skilled person nor an instructed person in the electrical-safety sense used by the definitions.
studyNote: The classification matters because some protective measures or access conditions depend on what electrical knowledge or supervision can reasonably be expected.

meaning: Reporting is communicating the results of periodic inspection and testing to the person who ordered the work.
studyNote: It is the communication stage that turns inspection and test findings into a usable record for the person responsible for the installation.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide links periodic inspection and testing with a report on condition and requires initial-verification results to be recorded in the appropriate certification and schedules.

meaning: A skilled person is someone with education, training and practical skills appropriate to the electrical work being undertaken and who can recognize electrical risks and avoid the resulting hazards.
studyNote: Competence is therefore task- and risk-dependent; the definition does not reduce it to possession of a particular title alone.
distinction: An instructed person works with adequate advice or supervision; an ordinary person is neither skilled nor instructed.

meaning: A temporary electrical installation is installed for a particular purpose and is intended to be dismantled once that purpose ends.
studyNote: Temporary does not mean exempt from safety requirements; it describes the installation's intended duration and purpose.

meaning: Testing is the use of appropriate test procedures and measuring instruments to assess an installation and prove characteristics that cannot be established by inspection alone.
studyNote: Typical verification tests establish continuity, insulation resistance, polarity, earth-fault loop impedance, prospective fault current and device operation as applicable.
distinction: Inspection observes and examines; testing measures or proves; verification brings the required checks together.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide sets out test safety, the sequence of tests, protective-conductor continuity, ring continuity, insulation resistance, polarity, electrode resistance, earth-fault loop impedance and prospective fault-current measurement.

meaning: Verification is the overall process of checking that an electrical installation complies with the relevant BS 7671 requirements, including inspection, testing and certification.
studyNote: It is the umbrella process: inspection and testing provide evidence, and the results are recorded in the required certification or report.
distinction: Testing is only one part of verification.

currentGuide.note: The 2026 On-Site Guide requires inspection and testing during erection and on completion before an installation is put into service, with results recorded on the appropriate certificate and schedules.
